tts: Every day, millions of people press a button that does absolutely nothing. You might have pressed it today.
It's the crosswalk button. In two thousand four, New York City admitted that out of about three thousand two hundred buttons, more than two thousand five hundred were fake.
The lights had long since switched to computer timing. But the buttons stayed, because removing each one costs hundreds of dollars.
But that's not the strangest part. The door close button in an elevator is often disabled too, so someone with a cane or a stroller has time to get in. Usually, only firefighters can make it work.
And in some offices, according to repair technicians, there's a thermostat on the wall that isn't connected to anything. People turn it, and they instantly feel warmer.
So why do they exist? Psychologists call it the illusion of control. Once you've pressed the button, waiting gets easier, and getting angry gets harder.
Without a button, you're just standing there, not knowing how long it'll take. With one, you've done everything you could.
So that button does work. Just not on the traffic light. It works on you.
